kinds.boundary: the participant's type system cannot express what the expectation needs; not a defect
kinds.unresolved: the participant returned no type rather than a different one
kinds.divergence: the participant can express the expected answer and gives another

no-string-with-length.what: Neither type system has a string carrying a length, so varchar<10> and fixedchar<5> cannot come back as declared. DuckDB has no fixed-size binary either and returns BLOB for fixedbinary<4>; DataFusion returns FixedSizeBinary(4) and differs only on the two strings.

duckdb-timestamp-is-microseconds.what: DuckDB has second, millisecond, microsecond and nanosecond timestamps and no others, so these precisions have nothing to come back as.

validator-does-not-resolve.what: The validator answers with an unresolved type class rather than a type. It is not a wrong derivation and not a limit of a type system: nothing was derived to compare.

emit-mapping-ignored.what: RelCommon.emit names the outputs and their order; the answer is the input's instead. Filed as duckdb-substrait-extension#267.

read-projection-ignored.what: ReadRel.projection masks the read's columns before anything else; the answer is the unmasked schema. Filed as substrait-python#264 for substrait-python; substrait-java#1280 is open for Isthmus.

grouping-key-nullability.what: A field grouped on by every set stays required; one absent from some set becomes nullable. The answers make all keys required, or all nullable. DataFusion's instance is filed as apache/datafusion#24968.

join-output-not-applied.what: Semi and anti return one side, mark one side plus a boolean, single both with the opposite made nullable. The answer is the two inputs concatenated whatever the type says. Filed as substrait-validator#580 for the validator.

setop-nullability-own-rule.what: The spec's Output Type Derivation table gives a pattern per operation; these follow one rule for all of them. Filed as substrait-validator#579 for the validator.

decimal-own-derivation.what: functions_arithmetic_decimal.yaml fixes precision and scale; these compute their own.

spark-decimal-result-nullable.what: Spark returns a nullable decimal from arithmetic over required inputs; the precision and scale are the spec's.

avg-over-integers-returns-float.what: functions_arithmetic.yaml declares avg:i64 with return i64?, truncating partial values; the answer is a float. Filed as substrait-io/substrait#1210.

acero-required-lost-above-a-read.what: Acero keeps required on a plain read - control_passthrough_rn matches - and loses it above any operation, so every column comes back nullable.

acero-drops-a-fixed-size-binary.what: Arrow has fixed_size_binary and DataFusion returns it for this case; Acero returns binary. The two string lengths in the same case are not expressible in Arrow, so only fixedbinary<4> is a divergence here.

duckdb-timestamp-precision-ignored.what: DuckDB has TIMESTAMP_S, TIMESTAMP_MS and TIMESTAMP_NS, and its reader rejects a precision above 9, so it reads the field; every declared precision still comes back as microseconds.
